title: How a car's differential works
caption:
Your outside wheel travels over two metres farther in every 90° turn. This little box of gears is why your car doesn't fight itself. 🔧
Save this for the next time someone asks what a diff does.
sources: Outside-wheel extra distance in a turn = turn angle x track width (pi/2 x ~1.5 m = ~2.4 m)
Open differential kinematics: carrier speed = average of the two side-gear speeds; torque split equally (standard bevel-gear differential theory)
Limited-slip differentials: clutch-pack and helical-gear (Torsen) types bias torque to the wheel with more traction
